newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish 5-yr fixed bond minimum price seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Polish 5-yr fixed bond minimum price seen flat.

text.p: The minimum price of Poland's 12-percent five-year bonds is expected to stay flat at Thursday's 200 million zloty primary tender, dealers said.
They said investors were likely to bid for up to 300 million zlotys of the bonds, due June 12, 2001 against the Treasury's 200 million zloty offer.
The maximum yield was expected to stay unchanged at 19 percent from the last auction on February 20.
"The maximum yield of the bonds is likely to stay flat at last auction levels," said Piotr Korcz, debt dealer at Bank Handlowy SA.
Dealers expected some interest in the bonds from longer-term foreign investors, who were likely to be drawn by good Polish fundamentals.

"Foreign interest in Polish longer term debt looks stable from the fundamental point of view, considering Poland's efforts to control inflation and current account," a dealer at a London-based bank said.
The paper was quoted at 18.95/18.90 percent on the secondary market.

But dealers said that for short-term investors, the five-year paper was not very attractive because of a thin secondary market and finance ministry statements there was no room for a near-term cut in the zloty devaluation rate.
"Recent signals from finance ministry and National Bank of Poland seem unlikely to affect debt instruments longer than one-year to maturity," said Marcin Rzechowski from PBI SA.
The settlement date of this auction is March 20, 1997.
